title: W1 fold is partial: the flush call-site ordering is still unpinned, yet comments/test/PR body claim it is "unit-pinned"
detail: The before-the-clear ordering lives at the audio_flush call site, which no test executes. Swapping flush_maybe_duck(a) and a.pending = {} keeps all 18 audio tests green while the duck silently never fires — the exact r1 W1 ordering half remains unpinned despite the claims.
recommended_fix: Either restructure so the drain+clear is one pure testable proc, or soften the wording in the comment, test comment, and PR body to match the spec's accurate "device-gated, manual verification" framing.

title: Spec's amended Tasks list omits flush_maybe_duck and bed_duck_ratio and mis-describes the trigger path — the drift class its own change log claims eliminated
evidence:
`bed_envelope_step` (pure envelope transitions), `bed_duck_trigger`
    (called from `audio_flush` via the `pending_any_plays` helper),
    `bed_duck_multiplier` (pure, capped at 1.0 — the duck never raises the
    bed), `bed_level` (pure: master × pause × duck), `pending_any_plays`;  — grep of the spec for "flush_maybe_duck|bed_duck_ratio" returns nothing (exit 1), yet both procs ship in app/audio/audio.odin:522 and :551; bed_duck_trigger is actually called via flush_maybe_duck (audio.odin:396, 522-526), not "via the pending_any_plays helper".
detail: The r1 change-log entry exists specifically to kill spec/code proc drift ("a reviewer diffing spec against code finds procs that don't exist"), but the amendment missed the two procs the r2 folds added (the W1 pin proc, the N3 parameterized ratio).
recommended_fix: Add flush_maybe_duck and bed_duck_ratio to the spec's Tasks/Code Map and correct the bed_duck_trigger call-path description.

title: Build script still raw-tracebacks on missing ffmpeg — the third leg of r1 finding 9 was not folded
evidence:
ffmpeg_ver = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-version"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30).stdout.splitlines()[0]  — repo-wide grep of the script for "which|FileNotFoundError|try:|except" returns nothing; the guards section (lines 47-62) covers only the vault WAV: "if not os.path.exists(SRC):
    raise SystemExit(f"vault WAV missing: {SRC} — see the vault README; never commit the WAV")".
detail: r1 blind-hunter finding 9 listed three raw-traceback paths; r2 folded the missing-WAV and sampwidth guards and the hang timeout, but a missing ffmpeg binary still raises an unhandled FileNotFoundError instead of the actionable SystemExit style used for the WAV.
recommended_fix: Add an existence check (shutil.which("ffmpeg")) raising SystemExit with an actionable message before the first subprocess call.
